items.title: Bill Allred interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: And they’d invite this guy in. Sonny Anderson was a big Disney Entertainment guy then.

ctx.x: And I really took to it. Because I hadn’t even started seventh grade yet was when our band program started. There was no sixth grade music back in 1940 something. And so I was playing “Jam On Home” you know which was bad for me because for me reading music came second or something I had to learn to do. I recall when I left Rock Island to — what I did, I had a chance to go out to Vegas a few times and I got to know Charlie Teagarden. At that time he was the secretary of the union in Las Vegas, but played in a lot…

Miami who was like the heavy piano player in Miami, a guy named Jack Keller. K-E-L- L-E-R. What a great piano player. On drums Ray McKinley. On bass Chubby Jackson. And I’m saying to myself holy shit, I mean like wow. I mean I played in the Navy band you know, so — when I was in the Navy from ’54 to ’57, so I met a few people but never got a chance to work with them. And so I played about an hour in the combo room. They said, “Do some more.” You know. And they’d invite this guy in. Sonny Anderson was a big Disney…
No, what did your family think about the whole thing?
